title: The Second Tube
verdict: Dante Locke was responsible for the disappearance of a cash receipt book.
intent: Dante Locke wanted to hide missing stall-fee payments.
The culprit needed delayed discovery so the object could pass the first search and be recovered later.
action_schema: Use role-specific access: the market treasurer moved the receipt book during the vendor count.
Remove a cash receipt book from its checked location.
Hide the item in a hollow scale-weight box.
Allow incomplete suspicion to fall on distractor suspects.
evidence_cues: a cash receipt book disappeared from a farmers market office during vendor registration.
The object was confirmed present before the relevant disturbance.
The disappearance occurred within a narrow time window because the stall-bell rang during an unscheduled vendor count.
The physical trace was green ink on the inside of the cash drawer.
The relevant tool or mechanism was a rubber stamp with green ink on the handle.
The item could be concealed in a hollow scale-weight box.
The hiding place required insider knowledge because only the market treasurer knew the scale-weight box had been emptied for repairs.
distractor_cues: a vendor angry about being assigned a poor stall
a food-truck owner carrying cash bags
A visible conflict is suspicious but insufficient without timing and mechanism.
A bulky object or nervous behavior is insufficient unless it explains the hidden container.
